title: 16 20 0 Fertilizer: Ammonium Phosphate for Palay and Mais at Planting
metaTitle: 16 20 0 Fertilizer: Ammophos Uses on Rice and Corn
metaDescription: 16 20 0 fertilizer, or ammophos, gives nitrogen and phosphorus at planting. See what is in the bag, when to use it on rice and corn, and what it costs.
excerpt: 16 20 0 fertilizer is ammonium phosphate, sold in the Philippines as ammophos. Each bag gives 16 percent nitrogen and 20 percent phosphate but no potash. Farmers put it on at planting, when young roots need phosphorus. This guide covers what is inside, when to use it on palay and mais, and how it compares with complete fertilizer.

heroImage.alt: Farmers transplanting palay seedlings, the stage when 16 20 0 fertilizer goes on as the basal dose

blocks.text:
Many farmers just call it 16 20 fertilizer. The price lists of the Fertilizer and Pesticide Authority (FPA) and the PSA call it ammophos, and they track it right beside urea and complete. It is a fertilizer with phosphorus and nitrogen together, which makes it a good first dose for a young crop.

But it has one gap you must plan around: zero potassium. Get that part right and 16 20 0 can save you money at planting.
What is in a bag of 16 20 0 fertilizer

The grade reads nitrogen, phosphate and potash, in that order. So a 50 kg bag holds 8 kg of nitrogen, 10 kg of phosphate (P2O5) and no potash. The nitrogen comes in the ammonium form.

Many 16 20 0 products are ammonium phosphate sulfate, which also carries sulfur. The Indian maker GSFC, for example, sells it as 16 20 0 13, with 13 percent sulfur. On the FPA list of registered fertilizers, some local brands declare about 10 percent sulfur and others declare none. So read the label if your soil lacks sulfur.
Atlas fertilizer and other brands

Atlas Fertilizer Corporation, a Philippine maker, sells its 16 20 0 as Atlas Super Gro. Atlas describes it as a source of nitrogen and phosphorus plus the secondary nutrients calcium and sulfur. Many other companies register their own 16 20 0 with the FPA, most of them for all crops. Compare the price per bag and the label, since the grade is the same. Our guide to [fertilizer brands and dealers](/blog/fertilizer-brands-and-dealers) has more tips.
Why phosphorus matters at planting

IRRI says phosphorus drives root growth, tillering, early flowering and ripening. It moves easily inside the plant but hardly at all in the soil. So phosphorus has to sit where the roots will grow, and it has to be there early.

That is why IRRI advises mixing all the phosphorus into the soil before the last puddling, or within 10 to 15 days after direct seeding. The PalayCheck guide of PhilRice gives the same window: 0 to 14 days after transplanting (DAT), or 7 to 10 days after sowing (DAS).
Signs of phosphorus deficiency in rice

items: Stunted, dark green plants with narrow, short and very erect leaves
Few tillers and thin, spindly stems
Late maturity, and in severe cases no flowering
Fewer grains per panicle and many unfilled grains

blocks.text: Fertilizer high in phosphorus: how 16 20 0 compares

blocks.caption: Nutrients per 50 kg bag and FPA national average price for September 14 to 18, 2026. Prices change every week.

blocks.text:
If you need a fertilizer high in phosphorus, DAP carries more than twice the phosphate of 16 20 0 in each bag. It also costs far more per bag. For most rice and corn farms, the real choice at planting is between 16 20 0 and [complete fertilizer 14 14 14](/blog/complete-fertilizer-14-14-14).

The trade looks like this. Two bags of 16 20 0 give 16 kg of nitrogen and 20 kg of phosphate for about PHP 3,507.42 at the September 2026 average. Two bags of 14 14 14 give 14 kg of each nutrient, including potash, for about PHP 3,805.84. So 16 20 0 gives more nitrogen and phosphorus for less money, but you must bring potassium from somewhere else.
How to use 16 20 0 fertilizer on rice

The Abonong Swak guide of PhilRice lists 16 20 0 as an option for the basal dose. For a target of 5 to 6 tons per hectare, it calls for 2 bags of 14 14 14 or 16 20 0 per hectare at 0 to 14 DAT, or 10 to 14 DAS. Urea follows at tillering, then urea with half a bag of muriate of potash later on. The same plans add rice straw and 10 bags of chicken manure or compost.

If you choose 16 20 0 for the basal, remember the potassium. PalayCheck times the first potassium dose at 0 to 14 DAT, the same window as the basal. On soils short of potassium, add [potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer) at basal as your soil test or technician advises. Our page on [fertilizer for rice](/blog/fertilizer-for-rice) shows the full season plan.

blocks.title: Mix it into the mud
blocks.text: Phosphorus does not move far in soil. Broadcast 16 20 0 evenly and work it into the mud during the last harrowing, so it sits where the new roots will grow.
How to use 16 20 0 fertilizer on corn

The corn guide of DA Regional Field Office 2 puts all the phosphorus and potassium, plus half the nitrogen, in the furrow at planting. The band goes about 5 cm beside and 5 cm below the seed, so the fertilizer does not touch it. 16 20 0 fits this basal job well, with muriate of potash added for the potassium.

The rest of the nitrogen goes on as a side dress 21 to 30 days after planting, during hilling up. [Urea fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer) usually does that job. For the rest of the crop, see [pagtatanim ng mais](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-mais).
Work out the bags for your farm

Say your plan follows PhilRice and uses 2 bags of 16 20 0 per hectare. For a 0.8 hectare lot, multiply 2 by 0.8 to get 1.6 bags, or 80 kg. For phosphorus from a soil test, divide the kilos of phosphate needed by 0.20. Our [fertilizer calculation](/blog/fertilizer-calculation) guide walks through each step.

blocks.text: Questions about 16 20 0

items.a: It is ammonium phosphate, often ammonium phosphate sulfate. A 50 kg bag gives 8 kg of nitrogen and 10 kg of phosphate, and some brands add sulfur.
PhilRice lists either one for the basal dose. 16 20 0 gives more nitrogen and phosphorus per bag, but no potassium. Use complete, or add potash, if your soil lacks potassium.
The FPA national average for September 14 to 18, 2026 was PHP 1,753.71 per 50 kg bag. In January 2026 it was PHP 1,460.84. Check the FPA list for your province before you buy.

items.q: What fertilizer is highest in phosphorus?
items.a: Of the common grades, DAP 18 46 0 has the most at 46 percent phosphate. Then comes 16 20 0 at 20 percent and complete 14 14 14 at 14 percent.

items.q: When do I apply 16 20 0 on corn?
items.a: At planting, in a band about 5 cm beside and 5 cm below the seed, as the DA Region 2 corn guide advises.
